_comment: CANONICAL per-chain token policy/registry — SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH. Consumed by the backend (app/services/router_registry.py) AND the Foundry config script (packages/contracts/script/SetFeeConfig.s.sol). Neither side is generated; both read this file so contract config and backend cannot drift. Fee model is FLAT (never %): flatFee below the EUR-1000-equivalent threshold, aboveFee at/above. flatFee=0.60, aboveFee=3.00, threshold=1000, each in the token's minimal units. surcharge passed on-chain = aboveFee-flatFee. permitType is STATIC policy (no runtime introspection): eip2612 -> permit flow (permitVersion is the EIP-712 domain version), none -> approve+pay. DAI=none is DELIBERATE (its permit is non-standard). assetType in {native,bridged}; issuer in {Circle,Tether,Maker} (omitted for native ETH). INVARIANT enforced in CI: enabled => verified (a token can NEVER ship enabled with verified=false); every address is EIP-55 checksummed. TWO-SIDED DISABLE: disabling a token requires BOTH enabled=false here AND setFeeConfig(token, enabled=false) on-chain — flipping only this JSON does NOT stop a direct on-chain pay(); SetFeeConfig.s.sol drives the on-chain enabled flag from this file. ADDRESS SAFETY: launch-set addresses were cross-checked vs official issuer docs (Circle/Tether/Maker) + explorers (verified=true); the deploy script additionally hard-gates each enable on the token's on-chain symbol()/decimals(); a human still eyeballs before mainnet. ROUTER V2 (fee-less, ownerless): the fee keys (flatFee/threshold/aboveFee) configure the v1 RSendsRouter ONLY. Chains served by RSendsRouterV2 ignore them (the backend reads only enabled/permit/identity there) and must NEVER be fed to SetFeeConfig.s.sol — v2 has no fee config and no owner to call it.

tron_nile._comment: TRON Nile testnet. Keyed by NAME like its mainnet sibling — a non-EVM chain has no EVM chain id and must not be given a synthetic one. TOKEN SELECTION: there are roughly fifty contracts on Nile calling themselves USDT and almost all of them are unobtainable, so the usual criterion (the issuer's canonical deployment) does not exist here. The only criterion that means anything on a testnet is whether a developer can actually GET the token: TXYZopYRdj2D9XRtbG411XZZ3kM5VkAeBf is what the official Nile faucet at nileex.io dispenses, decimals() read as 6 from the contract. If the faucet ever changes what it hands out, this address is wrong even though it will keep validating — re-check it against the faucet, not against a block explorer's token list. Fees are 0 like mainnet TRON: watch-only settlement never touches a router, so there is no fee to configure and nothing here is fed to SetFeeConfig.s.sol.
